newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares end lower on very slim turnover.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares end lower on very slim turnover.

text.p: New Zealand shares closed slightly weaker on Monday in what brokers said was one of the slimmest day's trading of the year.
Brokers said investors, particularly foreigners, continued to shy away following the meltdown on Wall Street last week and appeared unconvinced by the Dow's 49 point gain on Friday.
"It's hard to see in the short term anything that is going to enthuse the market," SBC Warburg broker Murray Rutherford said. "You could expect the market to drift a little bit lower."
JB Were & Co broker Luke Koekoek said the local market ccontiued to rely on foreign investors to take it forward.
"Not everyone was convinced by Wall Street's gain on Friday. If they are not there you could see the market drift lower."
The day's turnover was a paltry NZ$23.6 million and the top 40 share index fell 4.52 to 2,221.01.
Brewer Lion Nathan was one of the few highlights on the market with turnover of 1.37 million shares.

It ended five cents down at $3.38 but picked up a cent off its lows during the afternoon after managing director Doug Myers told Reuters its Australian breweries had picked up market share in the last two months.
Index heavyweight Telecom ended just one cent down at $6.56, up from a $6.53 session low, but on turnover of a weak 341,000.
Rutherford said the bearish tone had been somewhat alleviated by a recovery in local bonds, compared with general nervousness around many international bonds.
Fletcher Building fell seven cents to $4.24.
